test_title: SSC GD Constable Previous Year Paper (Held on: 15th December 2021 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: ₹16,000 is lent out for 2 years at 20% compound interest per annum. If the interest had been compounded half yearly instead of compounded annually, then ₹x more would have been earned as interest. What is the value of x?
solution:
**Given:**

Principle = 16000

Time = 2 years

Rate = 20%

If rate is six monthly then rate is increased in the form of x

**Formula used:**

A = P(1 + R/100)T

A = CI + P

**Calculation:**

A = P(1 + R/100)T

A = 16000(1 + 20/100)²

⇒ A = 23040 

CI = A - P

⇒ CI = 23040 - 16000 

⇒ CI = 7040

Now, if rate is six monthly

R = {20over 2}\% = 10%

T = 2 × 2 = 4 years

Now, 

A = 16000(1 + 10/100)4

⇒ A = 23425.6

CI = A - P 

⇒ CI = 23425.6 - 16000 

⇒ CI = 7425.6

Now, 

x = 7425.6 - 7040 

⇒ x = 385.60

**∴ The increased compound interest, x = Rs. 385.60**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] __Alternate Method__**

If rate is annually,

⇒ 16000 × 20% = 3200 × 2 = 6400

⇒ 3200 × 20% = 640 × 1 = 640

CI = 6400 + 640 = 7040

If rate is six monthly

⇒ 16000 × 10% = 1600 × 4 = 6400

⇒1600 × 10% = 160 × 6 = 960

⇒ 160 × 10% = 16 × 4 = 64

⇒ 16 × 10% = 1.6 × 1 = 1.6

CI = 6400 + 960 + 64 + 1.6 

⇒ CI = 7425.6

x = 7425.6 - 7040

⇒ x = 385.6

∴ The increased compound interest = x = Rs. 385.60
